content:
The initial idea with the ./QuantumInfo part of Physlib was to eventually merge it with the rest of the content. I currently don't see any progress in this direction. One suggestion that has been posed was to move the ./QuantumInfo stuff into ./PhyslibAlpha. I see two advantages of this:

  1. It reduces the overall complexity of the repository structure.
  2. It means we can more rapidly edit and fix e.g. liniting issues which are part of ./QuantumInfo.

Everything else would remain much the same - with a focus on moving the content eventually to ./Physlib.

I understand there may be some strong feelings on this, so wanted to gather peoples thoughts.

/poll Move QuantumInfo into PhyslibAlpha?
Yes
No

Would like to restart this discussion, I think it would be good to make this move into PhyslibAlpha as recently I had a look through the quantuminfo codebase and it is quite distinct from Physlib with its conventions. Ideally the read me should not have to explain a distinct code base in the folder structure when PhyslibAlpha exists; furthermore, with the interest in pointing AI directly at work within PhyslibAlpha, QuantumInfo might be a very good target for some tools/workflows especially on the matter of automatic upstreaming to Physlib from PhyslibAlpha.

I spoken with a number of people over the last week or so about this. I think the conclusion is that:

  1. Having the separate directory ./QuantumInfo in the long term is not ideal.
  2. However, there is not much harm having it present in the short term.
  3. Our effort should be focused on building a shared foundation of quantum in ./Physlib.

In terms of using AI to clean up and improve QuantumInfo I think this is currently welcome, and can be done in that directory.

Okay sounds good, point 3 seems to be quite important as there seems to be lots of independent work alongside quantuminfo in quantum physics that can then placed into physlib with this shared foundation.

I think in general it would also be good for us to work towards having physlib as the primary folder as connecting seperate results together in one library (with one set of conventions) is a big advantage of this monolithic style. Furthemore, it aids our commitment to maintenance as well :)
@Nathaneal Sajan : I've left a comment with a concrete proposal over at #Physlib > Integrating QuantumInfo.
Thank you @David Gross I really appreciate that, will engage on this topic in that thread :)
